Orrery

Orrery

A top-down model of the solar system. Every planet circles the Sun at its real relative speed, so you can watch the inner worlds lap the outer ones.

Orbit sizes are compressed and planets drawn much larger than life so everything fits. The order, the orbital periods and the relative speeds are real, and the planets start where they are today. Press space to pause.

Configurations

On the orrery, the yellow arc is the planet's true angle from the Sun as seen from Earth. Orbits are drawn compressed, so the arc can look different. Dates are approximate, typically within a few days.

Sky from the horizon

The date follows the orrery above. It starts at your location if the browser allows it, otherwise Leicester. The dashed line is the ecliptic, the path the planets follow. Faded planets are below the horizon. Orbital tilt is ignored, so positions can be a few degrees out.
